readings.title: The Dread of Mo’aḇ and the Summons of Bil’am
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging the Irrevocable Covenant Strength
readings.text: [Numbers 22:1] And the children of Yisra’ĕl set out and camped in the desert plains of Mo’aḇ beyond the Yardĕn of Yeriḥo. [2] And Balaq son of Tsippor saw <dn>את</dn> all that Yisra’ĕl had done to the Amorites. [3] And Mo’aḇ was exceedingly afraid of the people because they were many, and Mo’aḇ was in dread because of the children of Yisra’ĕl. [4] And Mo’aḇ said to the elders of Miḏyan, “Now this company is licking up <dn>את</dn> all that is around us, as an ox licks up <dn>את</dn> the grass of the field.” Now Balaq son of Tsippor was sovereign of the Mo’aḇites at that time, [5] and he sent messengers to Bil’am son of Be’or at Pethor, which is near the River in the land of the sons of his people, to call him, saying, “See, a people has come from Mitsrayim. See, they have covered <dn>את</dn> the surface of the land, and are settling next to me! [6] “And now, please come at once, curse this people for me, for they are too strong for me. It might be that I strike them and drive them out of the land, for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.”

readings.title: The Divine Refusal to Curse the Blessed
readings.subtitle: Elohim Rejects the Delegation of Spiritual Fraud
readings.text: [7] And the elders of Mo’aḇ and the elders of Miḏyan left with the fees for divination in their hand, and they came to Bil’am and spoke the words of Balaq to him. [8] And he said to them, “Spend the night here, and I shall bring back word to you, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> speaks to me.” So the heads of Mo’aḇ stayed with Bil’am. [9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Bil’am and said, <dq>“Who are these men with you?”</dq> [10] And Bil’am said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Balaq, son of Tsippor, sovereign of Mo’aḇ, has sent to me, saying, [11] See, a people has come out of Mitsrayim and cover <dn>את</dn> the surface of the land. Come now, curse them for me. It might be that I am able to fight against them and drive them out.’ ” [12] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Bil’am, <dq>“Do not go with them. You do not curse <dn>את</dn> the people, for they are blessed.”</dq> [13] And Bil’am rose in the morning and said to the heads of Balaq, “Go back to your land, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has refused to allow me to go with you.” [14] And the heads of Mo’aḇ arose and went to Balaq, and said, “Bil’am refuses to come with us.”

readings.title: The Escalation of Balaq and the Conditional Release
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Asserts Absolute Governance Over the Prophet’s Way
readings.text: [15] Then Balaq again sent heads, more numerous and more esteemed than they. [16] And they came to Bil’am and said to him, “This is what Balaq son of Tsippor said: ‘Do not be withheld from coming to me, please, [17] for I esteem you very greatly, and whatever you say to me, I do. Therefore please come, curse this people for me.’ ” [18] And Bil’am answered and said to the servants of Balaq, “Though Balaq were to give me his house filled with silver and gold, I am unable to go beyond <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, to do less or more. [19] “And now, please, you also stay here tonight, and let me find out what more <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> says to me.” [20] And <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Bil’am at night and said to him, <dq>“If the men come to call you, rise and go with them, but only <dn>את</dn> the word which <dn>I</dn> speak to you that you do.”</dq>

readings.section: The Architecture of the Opposable Agent
readings.title: The Right Arm Restricts the Reckless Path
readings.subtitle: The Physical Extension of YeHoVaH Intercepts Spiritual Rebellion
readings.text: [Numbers 22:21] And Bil’am rose in the morning and saddled <dn>את</dn> his donkey, and went with the heads of Mo’aḇ. [22] But the displeasure of <dn>Elohim</dn> burned because he went, and the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stationed <dn>Himself</dn> in the way as an adversary against him. And he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him. [23] And the donkey saw <dn>את</dn> the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> standing in the way with <dn>His</dn> drawn sword in <dn>His</dn> hand, and the donkey turned aside out of the way and went into the field. So Bil’am struck <dn>את</dn> the donkey to turn her back onto the way. [24] Then the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood in a narrow passage between the vineyards, with a wall on this side and a wall on that side. [25] And when the donkey saw <dn>את</dn> the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, she pushed herself against the wall and crushed <dn>את</dn> Bil’am’s foot against the wall, so he struck her again. [26] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went further, and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn aside, right or left. [27] And when the donkey saw <dn>את</dn> the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, she lay down under Bil’am. So Bil’am’s displeasure burned, and he struck <dn>את</dn> the donkey with his staff.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Opposable Agent
readings.title: The Unveiled Eyes and the Mandate of the Messenger
readings.subtitle: Submission to the Ultimate Authority of the Drawn Sword
readings.text: [28] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> opened <dn>את</dn> the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Bil’am, “What have I done to you, that you have stricken me these three times?” [29] And Bil’am said to the donkey, “Because you have mocked me. I wish there were a sword in my hand, for I would have killed you by now!” [30] And the donkey said to Bil’am, “Am I not your donkey on which you have ridden, ever since I became yours, to this day? Was I ever known to do so to you?” And he said, “No.” [31] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> opened <dn>את</dn> Bil’am’s eyes, and he saw <dn>את</dn> the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> standing in the way with <dn>His</dn> drawn sword in <dn>His</dn> hand. And he bowed his head and fell on his face. [32] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Why have you struck <dn>את</dn> your donkey these three times? See, <dn>I</dn> have come out to stand against you, because your way is reckless before <dn>Me</dn>. [33] “And the donkey saw <dn>Me</dn> and turned aside from <dn>Me</dn> these three times. If she had not turned aside from <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> certainly would have killed <dn>את</dn> you by now, and let her live.”</dq> [34] And Bil’am said to the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “I have sinned, for I did not know <dn>You</dn> stood in the way against me. And now, if evil is in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, let me turn back.” [35] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Bil’am, <dq>“Go with the men, but only <dn>את</dn> the word that <dn>I</dn> speak to you, that you speak.”</dq> Bil’am then went with the heads of Balaq.

readings.title: The Arrival at the High Places of Ba’al
readings.subtitle: Standing at the Extremity to Confront the Blessing
readings.text: [36] And when Balaq heard that Bil’am was coming, he went out to meet him at the city of Mo’aḇ, which is on the border at the Arnon, which was in the extremity of the border. [37] And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Did I not urgently send to you, calling for you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to esteem you?” [38] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “See, I have come to you! Now, am I at all able to say somewhat? The word that <dn>Elohim</dn> puts in my mouth, that I speak.” [39] And Bil’am went with Balaq, and they came to Qiryath Ḥutsoth. [40] And Balaq slaughtered cattle and sheep, and he sent some to Bil’am and to the heads who were with him. [41] And it came to be in the morning, that Balaq took <dn>את</dn> Bil’am and brought him up to the high places of Ba’al, and from there he saw the extremity of the camp.

readings.title: The Bare Height and the Exacting of the Word
readings.subtitle: Preparing the Geometric Framework for the Decree
readings.text: [Numbers 23:1] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Build seven slaughter-places for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.” [2] And Balaq did as Bil’am had spoken, and Balaq and Bil’am offered a bull and a ram on each slaughter-place. [3] Bil’am then said to Balaq, “Stand by your ascending offering, and let me go on. It might be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does come to meet me, and whatever <dn>He</dn> shows me I shall declare to you.” And he went to a bare height. [4] And <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Bil’am, and he said to <dn>Him</dn>, “<dn>את</dn> The seven slaughter-places I have prepared, and I have offered on each slaughter-place a bull and a ram.” [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> put a word in the mouth of Bil’am, and said, <dq>“Return to Balaq, and this is what you say.”</dq> [6] And he returned to him and saw him standing by his ascending offering, he and all the heads of Mo’aḇ.

readings.title: The Irrevocable Blessing of Ya’aqoḇ
readings.subtitle: The Prophetic Vision of a People Dwelling Alone
readings.text: [7] And he took up his proverb and said, “Balaq the sovereign of Mo’aḇ has brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east. ‘Come, curse Ya’aqoḇ for me, and come, rage at Yisra’ĕl!’ [8] “How do I curse whom <dn>Ēl</dn> has not cursed? And how do I rage at whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not raged? [9] “For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I observe him. Look, a people dwelling alone, not reckoning itself among the nations. [10] “Who shall count <dn>את</dn> the dust of Ya’aqoḇ, and the number of <dn>את</dn> one-fourth of Yisra’ĕl? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his!” [11] And Balaq said to Bil’am, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and look, you have kept on blessing!” [12] And he answered and said, “Should I not take heed to speak <dn>את</dn> what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has put in my mouth?”

readings.title: The Tactical Shift to Pisgah
readings.subtitle: The Futile Attempt to Fragment the View of the Covenant
readings.text: [Numbers 23:13] And Balaq said to him, “Please come with me to another place from where you see them. You only see the extremity but not all of them. Curse them for me from there.” [14] And he took him to the field of Tsophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven slaughter-places, and offered a bull and a ram on each slaughter-place. [15] And he said to Balaq, “Stand here by your ascending offering while I meet over there.” [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Bil’am, and put a word in his mouth, and said, <dq>“Go back to Balaq, and say this.”</dq> [17] So he went to him and saw him standing by his ascending offering, and the heads of Mo’aḇ with him. And Balaq asked him, “What did <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> say?”

readings.title: The Incorruptible Decree and the Wild Ox
readings.subtitle: Ēl’s Immutable Justice Prevents Reversal
readings.text: [18] And he took up his proverb and said, “Rise up, Balaq, and hear! Listen to me, son of Tsippor! [19] "<dn>Ēl</dn> is not a man, to lie; nor a son of man, to repent! Has <dn>He</dn> said, and would <dn>He</dn> not do it; or spoken, and would not confirm it? [20] “See, I have received, to bless. And <dn>He</dn> has blessed, and I do not reverse it. [21] “<dn>He</dn> has not looked upon wickedness in Ya’aqoḇ, nor has <dn>He</dn> seen trouble in Yisra’ĕl. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> is with him, and the shout of a Sovereign is in him. [22] "<dn>Ēl</dn> who brought them out of Mitsrayim, is for them like the horns of a wild ox. [23] “For there is no sorcery against Ya’aqoḇ, nor is there any divination against Yisra’ĕl. Now it is said to Ya’aqoḇ and to Yisra’ĕl, ‘What has <dn>Ēl</dn> done!’ [24] “Look, a people rises like a lioness, and lifts itself up like a lion; it lies not down until it devours the prey, and drinks the blood of the slain.” [25] And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Do not curse them at all, nor bless them at all!” [26] And Bil’am answered and said to Balaq, “Have I not spoken to you, saying, ‘<dn>את</dn> All that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> speaks, that I do’?”

readings.title: The Shift to Pe’or and the Alignment of the Spirit
readings.subtitle: Abandoning Sorcery for the Genuine Transmission of the Spirit
readings.text: [Numbers 23:27] And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Please come, let me take you to another place. It might be right in the eyes of <dn>Elohim</dn> that you curse them for me from there.” [28] And Balaq took <dn>את</dn> Bil’am to the top of Pe’or, that overlooks the wasteland. [29] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Build seven slaughter-places for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.” [30] And Balaq did as Bil’am had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each slaughter-place. [Numbers 24:1] And when Bil’am saw that it pleased <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to bless <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, he did not go as at other times, to seek to use sorcery, but he set his face toward the wilderness. [2] And Bil’am lifted up <dn>את</dn> his eyes and saw <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl encamped according to their tribes. And the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon him.

readings.title: The Abundant Tents of Israel and the Defeat of Aḡag
readings.subtitle: The Biological and Military Dominance of the Chosen Seed
readings.text: [3] And he took up his proverb and said, “The saying of Bil’am, son of Be’or, and the saying of the man whose eyes are opened, [4] the saying of him who hears the words of <dn>Ēl</dn>, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down, with eyes opened wide: [5] “How good are your tents, O Ya’aqoḇ, your dwellings, O Yisra’ĕl! [6] “Like wadis that stretch out, like gardens by a river, like aloes planted by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, like cedars beside waters. [7] “He makes water flow from his buckets, and his seed is in many waters. His sovereign is higher than Aḡag, and his reign is exalted. [8]

readings.title: The Final Rejection by Balaq
readings.subtitle: The Prophet Declares the Constraints of the Divine Economy
readings.text: [10] Then the displeasure of Balaq burned against Bil’am, and he struck <dn>את</dn> his hands together. Balaq then said to Bil’am, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, and see, you have kept on blessing, these three times! [11] “And now flee to your place. I said I would greatly esteem you, and see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has kept you back from esteem.” [12] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying, [13] If Balaq should give me <dn>את</dn> his house filled with silver and gold, I am unable to go beyond <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to do either good or evil of my own heart. What <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> speaks, <dn>את</dn> that I speak’? [14] “And now, see, I am going to my people. Come, let me advise you what this people is going to do to your people in the latter days.”

readings.title: The Star of Ya’aqoḇ and the Latter Days
readings.subtitle: The Coming Sceptre to Subjugate the Adversary’s Lineage
readings.text: [Numbers 24:15] And he took up his proverb and said, “The saying of Bil’am, son of Be’or, and the saying of the man whose eyes are opened, [16] the saying of him who hears the words of <dn>Ēl</dn>, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down, with eyes opened wide: [17] “I see <dn>Him</dn>, but not now; I observe <dn>Him</dn>, but not near. A Star shall come out of Ya’aqoḇ, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yisra’ĕl, and shall smite the corners of Mo’aḇ, and shall destroy <dn>את</dn> all the sons of Shĕth. [18] “And Eḏom shall be a possession; and Sĕ’ir shall be a possession – enemies – and Yisra’ĕl is doing mightily. [19] “And out of Ya’aqoḇ One shall rule and destroy the remnant from Ar.”

readings.title: The Prophetic Verdict on the Surrounding Nations
readings.subtitle: The Terminal State of Amalĕq, Asshur, and the Corrupt Order
readings.text: [20] He then looked on <dn>את</dn> Amalĕq, and he took up his proverb and said, “Amalĕq was first among the nations, but his latter end is to perish forever.” [21] He then looked on <dn>את</dn> the Qĕynites, and he took up his proverb and said, “Firm is your dwelling place, and your nest is set in the rock, [22] but Qayin is to be burned. Till when does Asshur keep you captive?” [23] And he took up his proverb and said, “Oh, who does live when <dn>Ēl</dn> does this? [24] And ships shall come from the coast of Kittim, and they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Ēḇer, and so shall Amalĕq, and he also perishes.” [25] And Bil’am arose and left, and returned to his place. And Balaq also went his way.
